# Rober González - Personal Portfolio

> Personal site for Rober González, Senior Software Designer focused on AI native products, working across product design, web design and data visualization. Based in Spain, working remotely.

The homepage is a single typographic page: a short first-person introduction where key terms (roles, disciplines, employers, clients) are set in bold or italic, and links carry a small icon. Some links show a small preview card on hover. It has light and dark themes that follow the system setting by default and can be switched manually.

The Lab collects experiments with that homepage: the same story and facts, told another way each time. Each experiment opens in a near-full-screen dialog on top of the Lab page.

## About Rober

- Senior Software Designer focused on AI native products, based in Spain, working remotely.
- Works across product design, web design and data visualization, from research to frontend code.
- Currently at Maisa AI, shaping how people work alongside Digital Workers.
- Fifteen years before that across startups (Fresh People), agencies (Populate) and enterprise (NTT Data), for clients like Santander, IAG, Acciona and Airbus.

## Lab

Works in progress, each a single HTML file. They are kept out of search engines (noindex) while they are experiments.

- [Open on the Canvas](https://rober.design/lab/canvas.html): The homepage as a design file you can pan and zoom, with frames, sticky notes and a layers panel.
- [Proof of Human](https://rober.design/lab/proof-of-human.html): The bio as a manuscript you can scrub back through keystroke by keystroke, with the crossed-out words kept in the margin. The tape currently shipped is a staged demo and is labelled as such on the page.
- [Colour Reference](https://rober.design/lab/wildcard.html): A paper fan deck whose palette is pulled live, in the browser, from Rober's portrait.

## Side Projects

- [Color Palette Extractor](https://www.figma.com/community/plugin/1513662449906068582/color-palette-extractor): A Figma plugin that pulls colours and gradients out of a design.
- [Should I Justify](https://shouldijustify.com/): A short case against justified text on the web.

## Related

- [Maisa AI](https://maisa.ai): Current employer, an AI software company.

## Technical Notes

- Stack: Vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no frontend framework and no build step.
- Self-hosted fonts, inlined icons and self-hosted link previews: pages load with no third-party requests, even on hover.
- Full content is in the HTML and renders without JavaScript. Without JavaScript, Lab experiments open as ordinary pages.
- Reduced-motion support via `prefers-reduced-motion`.
